scope: One original PLY-3 GUI Split/Extract and full public-MCP artifact download followed by GUI file reopen on the shared-index candidate.

result.observation: GUI Split and Extract, pre-reopen public-MCP Undo/Redo, project export, full public-MCP artifact download and GUI reopen completed. Public MCP core geometry digests for the extracted part, source and cutter matched the pre-reopen checks; the page reported no errors. The test removed its temporary downloaded file during cleanup.

extendedHistoryReplay.method: A separate run used the same production build and full-download GUI-reopen workflow, followed by actual GUI Undo and Redo with source, cutter and extracted geometry checks.
extendedHistoryReplay.ply1: The 274154-face PLY-1 control completed GUI reopen and post-reopen GUI Undo/Redo with matching checked geometry; reported peak 1359339520 bytes and cleanup confirmed.
extendedHistoryReplay.ply3: The 3691133-face replay completed Split, Extract and download, but GUI reopen timed out after 120 seconds before the new GUI history checks. The reported peak was 4548337664 bytes, above the 4294967296-byte strict threshold; cleanup confirmed. This failed run remains separate from the successful PLY-3 reopen above.

limitations: The successful run has approximately 35 MB of reported-peak headroom. The subsequent extended run timed out above the strict threshold, so repeatability and general resource bounds remain unestablished.
Undo and Redo used public MCP before reopening; GUI history controls, post-reopen history and public-MCP Extract were not exercised.
The streamed download hash was not independently compared to the original export artifact, and the temporary file was removed during cleanup.
No native Split output was compared. The open combined-preview cancellation timeout was not explained by the separate passing repeats; other M2 gates remain open.
Older failed over-limit and timeout receipts remain valid observations; this success does not identify the exact cause of their failures.
